ov: A large African antelope with a long face, oddly bent horns on both sexes, long legs and a back that slopes down from a hump over the shoulders. It grazes in herds of 20 to 300 on dry savannas and wooded grasslands, mainly in the morning and late afternoon.

why.et: A popular game animal because its meat is highly regarded.

ht: Just over 1 m at the shoulder
rg: Much of sub-Saharan Africa, from West Africa to Ethiopia and south to South Africa; now extinct in North Africa.
df: Mainly grasses, which make up at least 80% of its diet.
fx: When danger threatens, the whole herd flees in single file after one animal suddenly sets off.
The Bubal hartebeest of North Africa was declared extinct in 1994; the last one was shot in Algeria in 1925.
notes: RESOLVED (owner approved all suggestions, including the optional ones, 2026-09-29; ac left unchanged for eland, springbok and muntjac): ANSWER CHECK (fact): the lookout is confirmed ("one individual stays on the lookout for danger, often standing on a termite mound to see farther"), but the article gives no speed, so "one of the fastest antelopes" is unsourced.
